title: Toy Story 5 Breaks the Franchise's Own Records Overseas. In India, the Toys Came Home to a Half-Empty Room.
excerpt: Pixar's $275 million global juggernaut opened worldwide on June 19 — but Indian multiplexes gave Woody and Buzz a polite ₹1 crore shrug while a Bollywood love triangle ate their lunch.
body:
There is a particular kind of heartbreak that only a Pixar movie can engineer, and **Toy Story 5** spends two hours weaponising it. A tablet named Lilypad. Bonnie, now eight, too cool and too connected for the playthings she once dragged everywhere. Woody, voiced again by **Tom Hanks**, staring down the one enemy a cowboy doll can't out-loyal: a glowing screen. The toys have survived garbage trucks, daycare prisons and a literal incinerator. This time the villain is the thing in your child's hands right now.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=c51ND9Hdbw0</youtube>

The world showed up for it. **Toy Story 5** opened in theatres everywhere on June 19, and the early numbers are the stuff of studio dreams — a franchise-record preview night of roughly $13–14 million, the biggest of 2026, and a domestic opening tracking between $140 million and $185 million depending on which analyst you believe. Globally, Disney and Pixar are eyeing a $275 million debut weekend, the largest in the 31-year history of the series, eclipsing even *Toy Story 4*'s $249 million bow in 2019. Add a 94 per cent Rotten Tomatoes score and you have the rarest beast in 2026 cinema: a sequel nobody is rolling their eyes at.

> "The early box office tracking positions the film to outpace every previous entry — the highest opening in the franchise's history." — Variety, on Toy Story 5's projections

And then there is India, where Woody and Buzz walked into a near-empty room.

The fifth *Toy Story* opened to a muted **₹0.90 crore to ₹1.25 crore net** on its first day across the country — a number that would embarrass a mid-budget Hindi release, let alone the biggest animated franchise on earth. The film mustered around 2,461 shows, and occupancy told the real story: a national average hovering in single digits, with Mumbai at 11 per cent and the all-important morning shows actually *losing* to **Cocktail 2**, the Shahid Kapoor–Kriti Sanon–Rashmika Mandanna romance that bulldozed its way to a ₹10.86 crore opening the very same Friday. Pixar's toys, it turns out, are no match for a Bollywood love triangle in heat.

There was one bright spot, and it is the spot that always shows up for Hollywood in India: **Chennai**, where Toy Story 5 clocked a healthy 22.3 per cent occupancy, peaking at 33 per cent in night shows. The South, as ever, turns up for animation and spectacle while the Hindi belt yawns. Kochi, Bengaluru and Hyderabad held respectably; the Hindi-dubbed version barely registered.

Directed by Academy Award winner **Andrew Stanton** — the man behind *Finding Nemo* and *WALL-E*, which tells you he knows exactly how to make grown adults cry about machines — the film brings back the whole playroom gang, **Tim Allen** as Buzz Lightyear included, for a story that is openly anxious about the device-shaped hole in modern childhood. It is, in other words, a film that diaspora parents will recognise in their bones: the screen-time wars are universal, but they hit a little different when you are raising kids between two cultures and three time zones.

Which is why the India theatrical shrug barely matters for the people reading this. For Indian families in the **US, UK and Canada**, *Toy Story 5* is already playing on the biggest screens within driving distance — it opened in North America on 4,425 screens, blanketed UK and Canadian multiplexes the same weekend, and is the obvious Saturday-afternoon outing for anyone with a kid and a nostalgia streak the size of Texas. This is a movie built for the multi-generational living room: the NRI dad who saw the first one in 1995, the kid who has never known a world without a tablet, both of them ambushed by the same final-act gut-punch.

The streaming clock has already started ticking, too. Following Pixar's recent pattern, *Toy Story 5* is expected to land on **Disney+** roughly three to four months after its theatrical run — which puts a likely streaming debut somewhere around late 2026, comfortably in time for a winter-holiday rewatch in pyjamas. Whether the diaspora waits that long is another matter; this is a franchise people pay for in the dark, with overpriced popcorn, precisely so they can pretend the lump in their throat is the salt.

India's box office may have given the toys a cold welcome. But $275 million worldwide says the rest of the planet still can't quit them — and neither, if we are honest, can we.
